notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 22 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer222cont), the 25 weekly issues from 7 January to 24 June 1922. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1921-1924, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1922. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; 134 of the 201 rows read needed a name, a cost or the wording corrected, and a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out (where the crop shows only the heading, only the heading is published). Where a permit and its contract appear in the same issue the page carries one entry and the contract finding is held. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or engineer named is the owner or shares the owner's surname that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. Issue dates are set from the dated running heads, 25 issues one week apart with no gap. Permits whose heading counts more than one dwelling (11) were set aside before the image check and sit with the held single houses, as do nine single houses that were read against the image and have no architect left to name. Three held rows whose parcel has a page were read against the image and published.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 22 to 31 read (January 1922 to January 1932); the 14 half-year volumes before 1922 (1915 to December 1921) are unread, vol. 21 part 2 (July-December 1921, buildingengineer2921cont) next. In this volume: 172 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page (9 of them permits for a row of houses), are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but nine still need the image check). 249 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 982 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 2,677 numbered entries read, 1,596 San Francisco rows, 614 placed on a parcel, 201 picked and read against the page image, 158 published on 152 pages (95 seeded), 35 held back: twenty-six uses, storeys or unit counts that contradict the roll, six alterations listed by lot line with nothing to confirm the street number, two same-issue contracts and one listing of several buildings on a lot that is one parcel today; nine more joined the held houses.
